title: Making HTTP Requests with `requests` 📡
description: Send GET and POST requests, add headers, parameters, and handle responses with Python's requests library.

slides.title: Meet `requests` – HTTP for Humans
slides.content:
# The Most Popular Third‑Party Python Library

Install: `pip install requests`

```python
import requests
resp = requests.get('https://example.com')
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.text[:200])  # first 200 chars
```
Much simpler than raw sockets. It handles redirects, keep‑alive, and SSL automatically.

slides.title: First GET Request
slides.codeSnippet:
import requests
resp = requests.get('https://httpbin.org/get')
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.json())  # httpbin returns JSON

quizData.question: What does `resp.text` contain after a successful `requests.get()`?

options.text: The response body as a string

quizData.explanation: .text returns the raw content of the response (Unicode decoded).

slides.title: Query Parameters (GET)
slides.content:
# Pass a Dictionary to `params`

```python
payload = {'q': 'python hacking', 'page': 2}
resp = requests.get('https://example.com/search', params=payload)
print(resp.url)  # https://example.com/search?q=python+hacking&page=2
```
`requests` builds the query string for you, handling encoding.

slides.title: Sending POST Data
slides.content: Use the `data` parameter for form‑encoded data:
slides.codeSnippet:
import requests
resp = requests.post('https://httpbin.org/post', data={'user':'admin', 'pass':'1234'})
print(resp.json())

quizData.question: Using `data={'key':'value'}` in a POST request encodes it as JSON.
quizData.explanation: It encodes as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. For JSON, use `json={'key':'value'}`.

slides.title: Sending JSON
slides.content:
# The `json` Parameter

```python
resp = requests.post('https://api.example.com/login', json={'username':'admin', 'password':'secr3t'})
```
Sets `Content-Type: application/json` automatically.

slides.title: Custom Headers
slides.content:
# Masquerade as a Browser

```python
headers = {
    'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)',
    'Referer': 'https://google.com',
}
resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
```
Many web apps block scripts with the default Python User‑Agent. Always set a realistic one.

quizData.question: To set custom headers in a requests call, use the `________` argument.
quizData.explanation: The `headers` keyword allows you to pass a dict of HTTP headers.

slides.title: Error Handling with `requests`
slides.content:
# Use `raise_for_status()`

```python
try:
    resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
    resp.raise_for_status()  # raises HTTPError for 4xx/5xx
except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
    print(f"Request failed: {e}")
```
Always catch network errors to make your tools robust.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use a Session for Multiple Requests to the Same Host

```python
s = requests.Session()
s.headers.update({'User-Agent': 'Cybron'})
# now use s.get(...), s.post(...) – keeps cookies and connection pool.
```
We'll explore sessions later.
